## Headline

**Pipeline ACV reached $14.4M for Q3, up 12.4% vs Q2**. The best quarter on record for sourced pipeline, with win rate and pipeline coverage both moving the right direction. One yellow flag on retention. Everything else is green.

## What moved

ACV booked climbed steadily across the quarter. $845K in W27 to a peak of $1.41M in W37, broken only by a modest dip in the final week as deals slipped into October. Win rate ticked up 2.1 points to **38.2%**, and average deal size grew **4.8%** to $198K, consistent with the up market mix shift we have been pushing since Q1.

The one watchout is **GRR slipping 0.4 points to 93.9%**. The first sequential decline in five quarters. Root cause is three mid market expansion misses, not churn from the renewal book, which means it is recoverable rather than structural. Worth keeping in the recurring exec view but not yet a fire.

## So what

Pipeline coverage finished the quarter at **3.8x**. Comfortably above the 3.5x threshold heading into Q4. More importantly, the pipeline is not just bigger, it is better-shaped: Enterprise grew 4pts of share while SMB stayed flat, suggesting the up market motion is working as designed. Recommend extending the SDR AE pairing pilot from NAMER to EMEA next quarter. The unit economics support it.

## Talking points

- **Polaris Defense ($1.24M)** anchored Q3. Single deal accounted for 31% of the W36-W37 ACV lift. Treat it as exceptional in the comp narrative
- **APAC runs almost entirely through Partner channels** ($2.64M of $2.88M total APAC ACV). Healthy concentration but Partner risk is worth modeling for the Q1 plan
- **4.8% AOV lift is margin led, not discount led**. The pricing experiments we ran in Q2 held through volume. That is the real win behind the headline number
- **GRR dip is mid market expansion misses, not churn**. Three accounts (Acme, Helios, Vector) pushed expansions to Q4. Renewal book is healthy at 96.1%
- **EMEA Direct grew 18% QoQ**. Quietly the second best channel after NAMER Direct. Worth flagging for the EMEA review

## Risks + caveats

Pipeline coverage at 3.8x is a rolling indicator. Deal slippage in late September would compress the Q4 number quickly. We are already seeing two of the W39 forecasted closes push into October. The Polaris Defense deal also creates a **tough Q4 comp**: without an Enterprise outlier next quarter we would land 8-10% below Q3. Flag this in the Q4 plan so the board has the right shape of expectations. NRR dashboard view (separate cut, week over week) is the right next drill down before the QBR.
